'''''Christella dentata''''' is a small fern with widespread distribution in [[Australia]] and islands in the south [[Pacific Ocean]]. There are many local common names. In [[New South Wales]] it grows north from the southern [[Illawarra]] region and is known as '''binung'''.

Found on the margins of [[rainforest]], by streams or in more open forests with adequate moisture. [[Sorus|Sori]] are circular in shape,<ref>{{cite web |title=''Christella dentata''|work= PlantNET - NSW Flora Online|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Christella~dentata|access-date=2010-05-17}}</ref> with a hairy closed covering.

It was the first species of fern to become naturalised on the Hawaiian Islands, recorded initially in Oahu in 1887 and now found on all major islands there.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Brownsey |first1=Pat |last2=Perrie |first2=Leon |date=2016 |title=Re-evaluation of the taxonomic status of Christella dentata (Thelypteridaceae) supports recognition of one species in New Zealand |journal=Tuhinga: The Records of the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa |volume=27 |pages=51}}</ref> There it interbreeds with the local species ''[[Christella cyatheoides|C. cyatheoides]]'', with the resultant hybrid offspring sterile.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4ueqM7dgyj0C&q=Konrad+Christ+ferns&pg=PA85| page=85|title=Hawaiʻi's ferns and fern allies|author=Daniel Dooley Palmer| year=2003|publisher=University of Hawaii Press|isbn=0-8248-2522-5}}</ref>

''Christella dentata'' is an edible fern,<ref>Kumar M, Ramesh M, Sequiera S. Medicinal pteridophytes of Kerala, South India. Indian Fern J 2003; 20: 1-28.</ref> and also a folk remedy for skin diseases.<ref>Kumar S, Dash D. Flora of Nandan Kanan Sanctuary: Medicinal plants with their role in health care. Int J Pharm Life Sci 2012; 3(4): 1631-1642.</ref> Pharmacological study found that water extract of the fern was as toxic as the anticancer drug [[5-fluorouracil]] against [[chronic myelogenous leukemia|human chronic myelogenous leukemia]] cell line (K562).<ref>Chai TT, Yeoh LY, Mohd Ismail NI, Ong HC, Wong FC (2015) [http://www.ptfarm.pl/pub/File/Acta_Poloniae/2015/2/397.pdf Cytotoxicity and antiglucosidase potential of six selected edible and medicinal ferns]. Acta Poloniae Pharmaceutica - Drug Research. 72(2): 397-401.</ref>
